reviews.title: Reliable and Fast Industrial SSD for Demanding Use
reviews.comment: I purchased the ORICO Industrial 2TB M.2 NVMe SSD to install in an industrial workstation used for heavy data logging and virtual machine hosting. The drive is built to a higher industrial tolerance with durable components, which is exactly what I needed for a 24/7 application. Installation was straightforward — standard M.2 2280 format, recognized immediately by the system, and ready to format. Performance has been impressive, with sequential reads exceeding 5000 MB/s and writes around 4500 MB/s during testing. Random I/O is strong as well, which really helps with large file handling and virtual machines. Temperatures have stayed under control even with continuous workloads, thanks to its industrial-grade thermal design. There were no firmware issues, no crashes, and no compatibility hiccups on a modern PCIe 4.0 slot. For users who need a high-reliability NVMe solution with industrial-grade stability, this ORICO model is a practical and affordable choice. Pros: ✔️ Industrial-rated durability ✔️ Consistent, fast performance ✔️ Easy installation ✔️ Excellent for 24/7 workloads Cons: ➖ Premium pricing over typical consumer NVMe (but justified for industrial use) Overall, I would highly recommend this ORICO industrial SSD to anyone looking for dependable, high-performance storage in demanding environments.

reviews.title: Great Affordable TLC NAND NVME
reviews.comment: I normally don't leave reviews, but this one deserves it. Solid gen 4 NVME for the price, especially given the screw, heat sink, screw, and thermal is included. I tried a different model before this one, but the heatsink did not fit in my laptop. I have a very thin laptop, and this one sided ssd fit perfectly. So if you have a laptop,no worries. Chances are, this will fit. It has a TLC 232 NAND, a 2400 TW rating(4tb), a MAP1602 processing chip, and the build quality is top notch. The 7100 model comes with a TLC OR QLC, so I'd recommend this model. So far, temps have been steady and cool, but I'm not pushing it hard. I'm using it as a secondary drive, not a system drive. As far as longevity goes, that's to be determined as I've only used this for nearly a month. The company has a good reputation for dependable external drives, so hopefully this carries into their new NVME drives. The only downside I have is that their Amazon listing does not have as much product information as their website and there is an error in their description. Is says that the 4tb only has 1200 TW but on its website it states it has 2400 more than once. If you need a thin, fast, and affordable gen 4 NVME, this is a no brainer.
